ad_library.summary: 4 live Meta ads confirmed on 2026-11-21 on the Griffin Energy page (page ID 1421460234380992). Three started on 15 Nov 2026 and one on 4 Nov 2026. All four click to WhatsApp and all four carry the card footer 'Griffin Energy is a private installer'. The copy sells an EV-plus-rooftop angle (Rs.2.90 a km at a public charger vs 29 paise from the roof), the 31 March 2027 subsidy window, and Reliance HJT 715 Wp modules on Magnelis(R) steel. The website was read live the same day. Google Ads Transparency records were not checked in this pass.

funnel.destination: WhatsApp (wa.me / 'Send WhatsApp message') on all 4 ads
funnel.meaning: Every live ad sends the click to a WhatsApp chat rather than to griffinenergy.in. The site already has a free-survey form and a size-and-subsidy calculator, and none of this spend reaches either of them - so the click cannot be measured, retargeted or attributed.

findings: All 4 live ads click to WhatsApp ('Send WhatsApp message'), never to griffinenergy.in - so the site's own survey form and its size-and-subsidy calculator cannot measure, retarget or attribute any of this spend.

The ads promise 'subsidy and net meter handled for you', while the site's own FAQ still reads: 'Our registration on the national portal is in progress. We will show our vendor ID here once it is listed. Please ask us for the current status before you book.' The ad sells a service the site says is not yet in place.

Every ad card is stamped 'Griffin Energy is a private installer', but no ad, and no page, explains what that means for a homeowner's Rs.78,000 - a disclaimered ad that still promises the subsidy leaves the buyer to guess.

Three of the four live ads started on the same day (15 Nov 2026) and all four end at the same WhatsApp number, with no landing page and no UTM: the four creatives cannot be compared against each other or against anything downstream.

The site publishes the PM Surya Ghar slab (1 kW Rs.30,000, 2 kW Rs.60,000, 3 kW and above Rs.78,000) but not one system price, so the ad's 'subsidy handled' promise cannot be priced in a single click.

Nothing on the site - and nothing in any ad - names a customer, a review or a completed project count, on a purchase that runs to lakhs, while competing Hyderabad installers advertise install counts and reviews in the first line of the ad.
next_steps: Send at least one ad to griffinenergy.in, not only to WhatsApp
The site already has the better funnel - a free-survey form and a subsidy calculator. Put a Meta Pixel and UTMs on it and point one creative there so the click becomes measurable and retargetable.
Publish the PM Surya Ghar vendor status, or stop implying it

The FAQ says the portal registration is in progress. Until the vendor ID is listed, say in the ad exactly how the Rs.78,000 is claimed and by whom - the current copy reads as though Griffin claims it on the customer's behalf.
Put one worked price on the landing page
The subsidy slab is published but no system price is. Show one worked example - 3 kWp, on-roof, net of subsidy, with the EMI - so the ad's promise can be priced without a phone call.
Add the proof the ads are missing

One named Hyderabad install, one review, one kW figure. Griffin's technical story (Reliance HJT, Magnelis(R) steel) is stronger than most competitors'; the ad currently pairs it with no evidence that anyone has bought it.

site_audit.platform: Static single-page site, server-rendered HTML (hash anchors #quote / #calculator)
site_audit.scope_note: The website was read live on 2026-11-21 through a rendered-content fetch. Tracking-pixel and head checks (Meta Pixel, GA4, GTM, Google Ads, meta description, Open Graph, JSON-LD, favicon) need the raw served HTML and were not captured through this channel, so they are recorded as not checked rather than absent. PageSpeed and sitemap were not run.

issues: No live chat — missing after-hours leads
No visible testimonials/social proof on homepage

site_evidence.note: Head HTML not captured through the sandbox fetch channel; pixel presence is not checked, not asserted absent. No UTM parameters appear on any link in the rendered page content, and the ads themselves land on wa.me, which carries no campaign parameters.

promise_gap.promise: 'Subsidy and net meter handled for you' (3 of 4 ads)
promise_gap.site: The site FAQ says the PM Surya Ghar registration is 'in progress' and asks the buyer to check the current status before booking. The ad makes the same service sound settled.
The site says the scheme 'is currently funded until 31 March 2027'. The ad turns a funding window into a hard closing date - a claim a cautious buyer will check, and the page does not back it.

promise_gap.promise: 'Quoted in 24 hours. Installed in one day.'
promise_gap.site: The site repeats both, but qualifies the one-day install as applying 'once your approval comes through' and puts the real timeline at 6-9 weeks. The ad drops the qualification.

ads_audit.methodology: Control review follows the claude-ads Meta Ads audit catalog (github.com/vamsy16/claude-ads, ads/references/meta-audit.md). Each control is graded only where public evidence establishes it - Ad Library ad data and the lead's own landing page. Controls that require Ads Manager access (bidding, budgets, audiences, learning phase, EMQ, CAPI status) are marked unknown on purpose: they cannot be verified from outside the account and are never guessed.
